throughput_targets: Sustained 1,200 requests-per-second for chat endpoints (avg message length 240 tokens); peak bursts to 5,000 rps for 30 minutes - target 99th percentile throughput stability during 8-hour business window.
latency_slos: p95 per-token < 100ms on A100-equivalent machines; end-to-end response < 250ms for 1-3 turn chats (50-200 tokens); 99th tail considerations to be included in SLA addendum.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial reservation: 6 x A100-80GB (dedicated pool). Q3 scaling plan to 12 x A100; burst autoscale to on-demand 4 x A100. Want clear billing for burst vs reserved usage.
poc_summary: POC focused on performance + determinism for support chat and reranking pipelines. Ran synthetic load + representative prompt corpus (see prompts below). Key obs: batching and KV cache reduced nominal cost by ~32% vs baseline, but p95 latency drifted under sustained high concurrency without memory-tuned kernel flags. Need explicit kernel/quantization recommendation from Redwood for stable p95 at scale.
notes:
- Background: Glacial Ops is replacing a mix of in-house LLM endpoints and managed APIs for customer-facing chat + search rerank. High importance: predictable latency for live chat agents and SLA for enterprise customers.
- From kickoff call (Samantha Li + Diego): 'We need a measurable latency SLO before we make a 12-month commit.'
- Representative prompts used in POC (shortened):
  1) Support-chat: 'Customer: My shipment ETA changed, tracking shows error code 402. Give a concise reply, include next steps and escalation path.' (avg 80 tokens)
  2) Rerank: 8 candidate passages, score relevance to query "customs delay in port X" (avg 420 tokens total payload).
  3) Summary: multi-email thread (4 messages) -> 5-sentence executive summary.
- Load tests: ran three 2-hour soak windows at 1k, 2k, and 4k rps. Observed sustained throughput at 1k with p95 ~ 140ms after kernel tuning. At 4k needed additional reserved capacity and KV cache tuning to avoid p95 spike.
- Soak tests: 8-hour overnight soak at 1.2k rps showed memory leak suspicion on our internal orchestration (not Redwood runtime) — SE flagged.
- Security & compliance: completed SOC2 questionnaire; legal requested latency & availability SLA language be explicit (see SEC-4421).
- Cost sensitivity: procurement wants a blended unit cost target; need Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching to hit $0.002/token target for standard chat.
- Quotes and docs: BAFO waiting; pricing deck link in Drive.
- Customer quote on last call: 'If we can lock p95 and commit to an outage budget, we'll move forward with a 12-month reserved pool.'
- Misc: asked Redwood SE to run a targeted benchmark with 6-vs-8 KV cache warmups to measure warm-start latency (Diego follow-up).
